He played four years of [[college basketball]] at [[Duke University]], where he helped Duke win a [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national championship]] in 2015.{{cite web|title=Duke's Grayson Allen opens up on the tripping incidents that ruined his reputation|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2017/11/duke-basketball-grayson-allen-tripping-reputation|work=USA Today|date=November 8, 2017|access-date=October 27, 2021}} He has often been called one of Duke's best players of the 2010s.{{Cite web |last=Wittry |first=Andy |date=January 4, 2020 |title=The 11 best Duke men's basketball players of the decade |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2019-01-03/11-best-duke-mens-basketball-players-decade |access-date=December 27, 2021 |website=NCAA.com}}{{cite web|title=Duke Basketball's 2010s All-Decade Team|url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/ContentGallery/Picking-Duke-Basketballs-2010s-All-Decade-Team--148322766/#148322766_1|website=247Sports.com|access-date=December 27, 2021}} Allen was drafted with the 21st overall pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]], where he played for one season before being traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in July 2019. In August 2021, Allen was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], where he played for two seasons before being traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in September 2023. ==High school career== [[File:20140402 MCDAAG Grayson Allen dunk (2).JPG|thumb|right|Allen dunking in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] In 2014, Allen was selected as a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] out of [[Providence School]] in [[Jacksonville, Florida]], where he won a state championship the previous year.{{cite web |author=Borzello, Jeff |date=January 1, 2013 |title=Players announced for McDonald's All-American Game |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24424133/players-announced-for-mcdonalds-all-american-game |url-status=dead |access-date=November 20, 2014 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304032151/http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24424133/players-announced-for-mcdonalds-all-american-game }} He won the McDonald's All-American Slam Dunk Contest, jumping over future Duke teammate [[Jahlil Okafor]].{{cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/highschool-prep-rally/grayson-allen-leaps-over-6-foot-10-jahlil-okafor-to-win-mcdonald-s-dunk-contest-183314008.html|title=Grayson Allen leaps over 6-foot-10 Jahlil Okafor to win McDonald's dunk contest|work=Yahoo! Sports|first=Ben|last=Rohrbach|date=April 2, 2014|access-date=April 7, 2015}} ==College career== === Freshman season (2014–2015) === During Allen's freshman season at Duke, he averaged 4.4 points per game and was named to the ACC all-academic team.{{cite web |title=Grayson Allen Bio |url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/grayson-allen/4426 |access-date=January 3, 2025 |website=goduke.com}} Allen became a major contributor in the NCAA tournament. On April 7, 2015, he helped Duke to victory in the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|NCAA championship game]], scoring 16 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400788981|title=Comeback! Duke dispatches Wisconsin to capture national title No. 5|work=ESPN|date=April 6, 2015|access-date=April 7, 2015}} After the game, commentators cited Allen as one of the main reasons for Duke's win.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2015/04/06/duke-wisconsin-national-championship-final-four-ncaa-tournament/25386447/|title=Duke edges Wisconsin to win fifth national championship|first=Paul|last=Myerberg|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 7, 2015|access-date=April 7, 2015}} Coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] agreed, saying, "We were kind of dead in the water. We were nine points down and Grayson just put us on his back."{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/tourney/2015/04/06/duke-wisconsin-final-four-ncaa-tournament-championship-march-madnessgrayson-allen-tyus-jones-mike-krzyzewski/25386537/|title=Duke freshmen give Blue Devils late boost for title|first=Dan|last= Wolken|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 7, 2015|access-date=April 7, 2015}} === Sophomore season (2015–2016) === Allen received national attention following an incident during a game against [[Louisville Cardinals basketball|Louisville Cardinals]]. On February 8, 2016, Allen was assessed a [[Flagrant foul#ncaa-flagrant1|flagrant-one foul]] after he tripped Louisville forward [[Ray Spalding]]. Commentators said the move appeared to be intentional, as Allen stuck out his leg while on the ground as Spalding was hopping over him.{{cite web |last=Vecenie |first=Sam |title=WATCH: Duke's Grayson Allen trips Louisville player, gets flagrant foul |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/watch-dukes-grayson-allen-trips-louisville-player-gets-flagrant-foul/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=July 6, 2019 |language=en |date=February 8, 2016}}{{cite web |last=O'Neil |first=Dana |date=February 9, 2016 |title=Grayson Allen and being a hated white player with the Duke Blue Devils |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/14644805 |access-date=March 20, 2017 |website=ESPN}} In Duke's second game against Louisville, Allen exchanged elbows while scuffling for the ball and was later ejected for yelling at a referee after being called for his fifth foul.{{cite web |last=Brown |first=Mike |url=http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/165017632/duke-meltdown-issues-louisville-recap |title=A late meltdown at Louisville re-exposed Duke's issues |publisher=Sports on Earth |date=February 20, 2016 |access-date=March 20, 2017 |archive-date=February 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202001106/http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/165017632/duke-meltdown-issues-louisville-recap }} On February 25, in the closing seconds of a 15-point win against [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], Allen tripped opposing guard [[Xavier Rathan-Mayes]].{{cite web |date=February 27, 2016 |others=Contributed by [[Andy Katz]] and C.L. Brown |title=Grayson Allen of Duke Blue Devils won't be suspended by ACC for apparent trip |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/14853209 |access-date=March 20, 2017 |website=ESPN}} A day later, Allen received a reprimand from the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) for his second tripping incident in less than a month.{{Cite web |last=Waters |first=Mike |date=February 26, 2016 |title=ACC reprimands Duke's Grayson Allen |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2016/02/acc_reprimands_dukes_grayson_allen_for_tripping_florida_state_player.html |access-date=January 3, 2025 |website=syracuse.com}} During the 2015–16 season, Allen was one of the best offensive players in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]], averaging 21 points per game{{cite web|title=Atlantic Coast Conference Statistics – College Basketball – ESPN|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/2/acc-conference|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101220031735/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/2/acc-conference|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 20, 2010|website=ESPN.com|access-date=February 9, 2016}} and shooting 41% from three-point range. He played an average of 36.6 minutes per game and made 83.7% of his free throws.{{cite web|title=Atlantic Coast Conference Statistics – College Basketball – ESPN|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/2/stat/scoring-per-game/sort/threePointFieldGoalPct/acc-conference|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130216104007/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/2/stat/scoring-per-game/sort/threePointFieldGoalPct/acc-conference|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 16, 2013|website=ESPN.com|access-date=February 9, 2016}} In the NCAA tournament, Allen scored 29 points in Duke's 71–64 win over Yale, helping the team to reach the Sweet Sixteen.{{Cite web |last=McMillen |first=Gabrielle |date=March 19, 2016 |title=Grayson Allen dominates as Duke survives Yale in Round of 32 |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/duke-yale-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-round-of-32-grayson-allen/1vcyu6svd20f615jw41t8t3lzs |access-date=January 3, 2025 |website=sportingnews.com}} The team lost its next game to top-seeded Oregon, 82–68; Allen had difficulty scoring near the basket during that game,{{cite web |last=Keeley |first=Laura |date=March 25, 2016 |title=Duke's season ends in Sweet 16 with 82–68 loss to Oregon |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/duke/article68195347.html |access-date=January 3, 2025 |work=News Observer}} finishing with 15 points.{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2016/03/25/oregon-duke-sweet-16-ncaa-tournament/82243032/|title=Top-seeded Oregon knocks out defending champ Duke|first=Josh|last=Peter|website=USA TODAY}} === Junior season (2016–2017) === Entering his junior season, Allen was considered one of the top returning players in college basketball. He was named to the [[Associated Press]] preseason All-America team{{cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/duke-s-allen-leads-ap-preseason-all-america-team-110216 |title=Duke's Allen leads AP preseason All-America team |work=[[Foxsports.com]] |date=November 2, 2016 |access-date=November 12, 2016}} and was the ACC media's pick as preseason ACC Player of the Year.{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Norlander |url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/duke-the-pick-to-win-a-loaded-acc-grayson-allen-is-preseason-player-of-the-year/ |title=Duke the pick |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400915431 |access-date=February 9, 2017 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} Prior to the start of the season, Allen stated that basketball|Elon]]'s Steven Santa Ana and was charged with a technical foul.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/video/clip/_/id/18328374 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161222060404/http://www.espn.com/video/clip/_/id/18328374 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 22, 2016 |title=Grayson Allen gets a tech for tripping again |website=ESPN |date=December 21, 2016 |access-date=March 20, 2017}}{{cite web |date=December 21, 2016 |title=Grayson Allen reacts to getting called for a Technical Foul after tripping a player |url=https://www.espn.com/video/clip?id=18328343 |access-date=January 5, 2025 |website=ESPN}} The next day, Duke coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] suspended Allen from the team indefinitely. After Duke's December 31 game, Krzyzewski stripped Allen of his team captaincy.{{cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/acc/2016/12/22/duke-mike-krzyzewski-suspends-grayson-allen-indefinitely/95742040/ |title=Duke's Mike Krzyzewski suspends Grayson Allen indefinitely |first=Nicole |last=Auerbach |work=USA Today |date=December 22, 2016 |access-date=December 22, 2016}}{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/12/31/duke-grayson-allen-no-longer-team-captain |title=Duke's Grayson Allen stripped of captaincy after suspension for tripping |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=December 31, 2016 |access-date=January 5, 2017}} Allen returned to play on January 4, 2017, after serving a one-game suspension.{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/grayson-allen-suspension-duke-kicking-mike-krzyzewski-coach-k-joke-indefinite-010417 |title=What a joke! Coach K ends Grayson Allen's 'indefinite suspension' after just one game |first=Chris |last=Chase |work=Fox Sports |date=January 4, 2017 |access-date=January 5, 2017}} During the 2016–2017 season, Allen averaged 14.5 points per game and shot 36.5% from three-point range. He averaged 29.6 minutes per game and shot 81.1% from the free-throw line.{{cite web |title=Grayson Allen |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3135045 |access-date=January 4, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}} Duke reached the second round of the NCAA tournament, where the team was upset by South Carolina; Allen scored 20 points in the defeat.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/400947225|title=South Carolina vs. Duke – Game Recap – March 19, 2017 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com}} === Senior season (2017–2018) === [[File:DUKEvUNC 2018-03-03 - Mike Krzyzewski hugs Grayson Allen 1.jpg|thumb|right|230px|[[Mike Krzyzewski|Coach K]] embraces Allen at the end of his final home game at [[Duke University]].]] On April 18, 2017, it was announced Allen would return to Duke for his senior season.{{Cite web |last=Goodman |first=Jeff |date=April 18, 2017 |title=Grayson Allen coming back to Duke for senior season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19187876 |access-date=April 18, 2017 |website=ESPN.com |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}} The team voted to restore him as captain for the 2017–18 season.{{cite news |last=Bieler |first=Des |date=October 2, 2017 |title=Grayson Allen regains Duke captaincy lost after tripping incidents |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/early-lead/wp/2017/10/02/grayson-allen-regains-duke-captaincy-lost-after-tripping-incidents/ |access-date=January 3, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}} On November 14, 2017, Allen scored 37 points in an 88–81 win against [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986058|title=Allen leads No.1 Duke past No.2 Michigan State|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=November 14, 2017}} On November 29, 2017, Allen scored 21 points in a 91–81 victory over [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]].{{Cite On December 2, 2017, Allen scored 25 points and 3 rebounds in a 96–80 win against South Dakota.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986114|title=No.1 Duke beats South Dakota to improve to 10–0|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=December 2, 2017}} On December 30, 2017, Allen scored 22 points and 3 rebounds in a 100–93 win over [[Florida State FSU|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=December 30, 2017}} For the season, Allen averaged 15.5 points per game on 41.8% shooting.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/grayson-allen-1.html|title=Grayson Allen College Stats|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}} On March 9, 2018, Allen was assessed a flagrant-one foul in the [[ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] for tripping [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]'s Garrison Brooks with what was called a "hip check."{{Cite news |last=Schwartz |first=Nick |date=March 10, 2018 |title=See the controversial play that earned Grayson Allen a flagrant foul |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2018/03/see-the-controversial-play-that-earned-grayson-allen-a-flagrant-foul |access-date=January 3, 2025 |work=USA Today |language=en}} Duke reached the Elite Eight in the NCAA tournament, where the team was defeated by [[2017-18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]], 85–81, in overtime.{{Cite web |last=Schroeder |first=George |date=March 25, 2018 |title=NCAA tournament: Kansas breaks through to Final Four with overtime defeat of Duke |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/03/25/ncaa-tournament-kansas-takes-down-duke-get-back-final-four/457246002/ |access-date=January 3, 2025 |website=USA Today}} In his final collegiate game, Allen scored 12 points on 3-for-13 shooting, missed a potential game-winning shot, and missed two three-pointers late in overtime; he did, however, make several clutch free throws. Scott Gleeson of ''USA Today'' commented that the season "was a resurgent one for Allen as a whole, in spite of the sour ending. He took on the role of senior captain on a young team full of NBA talent. It was a flipped script from a year ago when Allen was seen as the villain of the sport for his unsportsmanlike behavior..."{{Cite web |last=Gleeson |first=Scott |date=March 25, 2018 |title=Duke falters in Elite 8 loss to Kansas, and Grayson Allen's polarizing career is over |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/03/25/duke-falters-elite-8-loss-kansas-and-now-grayson-allens-career-over/457402002/ |access-date=January 3, 2025 |website=USA Today}} ===Overall career=== During his four seasons at Duke, Allen appeared in 142 games and averaged 14.1 points, 3.2 rebounds and 3.0 assists. He maintained a field-goal percentage of .430, a three-point field-goal percentage of .380, and a free-throw percentage of .834. Allen finished his Duke career with 1,996 points, ranking 12th on the Blue Devils' career scoring list. Allen played in 15 NCAA tournament games, helping the Blue Devils win the 2015 NCAA national championship. He earned All-America and Academic All-America honors in 2016, becoming the sixth Blue Devil to receive both honors in the same season. Allen also earned All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Academic honors four times.{{Cite web|url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/grayson-allen/4426|title=Grayson Allen bio – Duke University|website=GoDuke.com|access-date=August 10, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2018–2019)=== [[File:Grayson Allen Utah (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|150px|Allen with the [[Utah Jazz]] in 2018]] On June 21, 2018, Allen was selected with the 21st overall pick by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. On July 2, Allen signed a four-year rookie scale contract with the Jazz.{{cite news|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2018/06/22/jazz-select-dukes-grayson-allen-no-21-overall/|title=Jazz select Duke's Grayson Allen No. 21 overall, earning Donovan Mitchell's approval|newspaper=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|last=Goon|first=Kyle|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=June 22, 2018}} He made his NBA debut on October 22, against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], scoring 7 points in 11 minutes off the bench.{{cite news |last=De Jong |first=Zach |title=Duke in the NBA: Grayson Allen shines in NBA debut |url=https://balldurham.com/2018/10/23/duke-in-the-nba-grayson-allen-shines-in-nba-debut/ |access-date=October 23, 2018 |work=Ball Durham |date=October 23, 2018}} On April 10, 2019, Allen scored a career-high 40 points with seven rebounds, four assists, a steal and a block in a 137–143 overtime loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071902|title=Clippers beat Jazz 143–137 in OT to stop 3-game skid on the final day of the season.|agency=Associated Press |date=April 10, 2019|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 11, 2019}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2019–2021)=== On July 6, 2019, Allen was traded, alongside [[Jae Crowder]], [[Kyle Korver]], the draft rights to [[Darius Bazley]] and a future first-round pick, to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Mike Conley Jr.|Mike Conley]].{{cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Grayson Allen, Jae Crowder, Kyle Korver, draft Allen hits game-winner in OT to beat Raptors] ===Phoenix Suns (2023–2026)=== On September 27, 2023, Allen, alongside [[Portland Trail Blazers]] players [[Jusuf Nurkić]], [[Nassir Little]] and [[Keon Johnson (basketball, born 2002)|Keon Johnson]], was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] as part of a three-team trade that sent [[Damian Lillard]] to the Milwaukee Bucks and [[Jrue Holiday]], [[Deandre Ayton]], [[Toumani Camara]] and a 2029 first-round draft pick to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=SUNS ACQUIRE NURKIĆ, ALLEN, LITTLE, JOHNSON|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-acquire-nurkic-allen-little-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2023|access-date=September 27, 2023}} On November 6, Allen scored a season-high 26 points as a starter with a career-high 8-of-13 three-pointers made in a tense 116–115 overtime win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/game/phx-vs-chi-0022300162/box-score | title=Phoenix Suns vs Chicago Bulls Nov 8, 2023 Box Scores | website=[[NBA.com]] }} On Christmas Day, Allen scored a new season high with 32 points made as a starter while making 8/17 three-pointers in a loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. On January 5, 2024, Allen scored 31 points with a new career-high 9-of-14 three-pointers made in a 113–97 win over the [[Miami Heat]]. The three-pointers made that game tied a franchise record previously set multiple times between former Suns players [[Quentin Richardson]], [[Channing Frye]], [[Aron Baynes]], [[Cameron Johnson]], and [[Landry Shamet]].{{cite web | url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2024/1/5/24027481/suns-vs-heat-final-score-grayson-allen-ties-suns-record-nine-made-three-pointers-cool-heat-113-97 | title=Suns vs. Heat Final Score: Grayson Allen ties Suns record with nine made three-pointers, Suns cool Heat 113-97 | date=January 5, 2024 }} He later tied his three-point record for a single game eleven days later; that game led to him only scoring 27 points that time, but he was a key contributor to a historic game where the Suns had a 22-point fourth-quarter comeback and 32-8 late game comeback stretch to upset the [[Sacramento Kings]] and win 119–117 at home.{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585195 | title=Suns 119-117 Kings (Jan 16, 2024) Game Recap }} On February 8, Allen broke his career high in assists by the end of the first half; he later finished with a career-high 14 assists in a 129–115 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/game/uta-vs-phx-0022300739 | title=Utah Jazz vs Phoenix Suns Feb 8, 2024 Game Summary | website=[[NBA.com]] }} On March 7, Allen put up 28 points on eight three-pointers made, with 21 points coming in the first quarter which set a career high for points in a quarter, in a 120–113 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/suns-news-unconscious-grayson-allen-sets-franchise-record-with-insane-3-point-shooting-vs-raptors|title=Suns: Unconscious Grayson Allen sets franchise record with 76ers vs Phoenix Suns Mar 20, 2024 Game Summary | website=[[NBA.com]] }} By the end of his first season with the Suns, Allen led the NBA in three-point shooting percentage with a 46.1% rating that He became the second Suns player behind [[Craig Hodges]] (and first player to be with the team throughout an entire season) to lead the NBA in three-point field goal shooting percentages in a season.{{cite web | url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2024/4/18/24133723/kevin-durant-and-devin-booker-produced-some-unique-statistics-this-season-phoenix-suns | title=Kevin Durant and Devin Booker produced some unique statistics this season | date=April 18, 2024 }} On April 15, 2024, Allen signed a four-year, $70 million extension with Suns.{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |language=en}} On February 7, 2025, Allen had 21 points, 7 rebounds and 6 assists in a 135-127 overtime win over the [[2024–25 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]]. In the final 4.4 seconds of regulation, Allen scored 6 points on 2 3-pointers, including a buzzer-beater that tied the game at 122 going into overtime.{{Citeweb|url=https://www.si.com/nba/suns/news/devin-booker-wants-stick-phoenix-suns-|title=Suns Survive in Overtime vs Jazz after Grayson Allen's Late Heroics|last=Mau|first=Brendan|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=February 8, 2025|accessdate=February 8, 2025}} On November 10, 2025, Allen put up a career-high 42 points on 10-of-15 three-point shooting in a 121–98 win over the [[2025–26 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]]. His 10 three-pointers made set a Suns franchise record for the most three-pointers made in a game.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/phoenix-suns/suns-news-grayson-allen-shatters-phoenixs-single-game-record-for-3s|title=Grayson Allen shatters Suns’ single-game record for 3s|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=November 10, 2025|access-date=November 11, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/grayson-allens-career-night-leads-suns-over-pelicans-121-98|title=Grayson Allen's Career Night Leads Suns Over Pelicans, 121-98|website=nba.com|last=Young|first=Shane|date=November 10, 2025|access-date=November 11, 2025}} Allen ended the season averaging a career-high 16.5 points per game, helping the Suns achieve a 45–37 record and the eighth seed in the playoffs, although Allen did not play in either of the team's play-in tournament games due to a left hamstring strain.{{Cite web |title=Phoenix Suns reveal injury status for Mark Williams and Grayson Allen ahead of Game 1 vs. Thunder |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/phoenix-suns-reveal-injury-status-174134699.html |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=Yahoo Sports}} The Suns faced the reigning champion and top-seeded [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] during their first round playoff series. After missing the first two games due to injury, Allen returned in Game 3, recording seven points in a 121–109 loss.{{Cite web |title=GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER SCORES 42, THUNDER BEAT SUNS 121-109 TO TAKE A 3-0 SERIES LEAD|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500143|access-date=May 1, 2026|website=NBA.com}} The Suns would end up being swept by the Thunder in four games. ===Charlotte Hornets (2026–present)=== On July 13, 2026, Allen, [[Royce O'Neale]] and a 2033 first-round pick were traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Miles Bridges]], a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-acquire-allen-oneale-first-round-pick|title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Allen, O’Neale, First Round Pick|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2026}} == Personal life == Allen began dating [[Morgan Reid]] while both were students at Duke.
